name: Step-by-Step Kitchen Drywall Restoration After a Plumbing Leak

step.name: Step 1: Stop the water source and inspect the cavity
step.text: Before touching any drywall, make sure the plumbing leak is fully resolved and no water is running. Check inside the wall cavity around the damaged area to confirm framing, wiring, and insulation are accounted for before starting removal.

step.name: Step 2: Cut away all soft and water-damaged drywall
step.text: Use a utility knife or jab saw to cut out the softened, water-stained section back to solid framing studs. Take out any wet insulation as well, because leaving damp material sealed inside wall cavities invites hidden mold growth.

step.name: Step 3: Allow the wall cavity to dry completely
step.text: Do not rush to hang new board while the interior framing remains damp to the touch. Run ventilation and verify the cavity is fully dried out so moisture does not get trapped behind your fresh patch.

step.name: Step 4: Measure and fasten a matching drywall piece
step.text: Measure the cutout precisely and screw in a matching thickness drywall piece directly into the exposed wall studs. Keep the fasteners countersunk just slightly beneath the paper face without tearing through the core.

step.name: Step 5: Tape joints and apply your initial compound coat
step.text: Cover all perimeter seams with joint tape and lay down your initial layer of joint compound across the tape and screw heads. Feather the edges out wide so the patch blends smoothly across the surrounding wall plane.

step.name: Step 6: Sand smooth and replicate the kitchen texture
step.text: Once completely dry, sand the patched area smooth and match the surrounding kitchen wall texture using proper compound techniques. A smooth texture match ensures the repaired spot blends naturally with adjacent surfaces.

step.name: Step 7: Apply stain-blocking primer and kitchen-grade finish paint
step.text: Seal the repaired patch thoroughly with primer before applying durable, moisture-resistant kitchen paint. Priming prevents joint compound from absorbing the paint unevenly or showing visible flashing under kitchen lighting.
